The answer to "when did the first settlers arrive" depends on the scope and definition of "settlers." The first settlers of North America overall arrived between 19,000 and 26,000 years ago as nomadic hunter-gatherers [d5]. For European settlers specifically, the Spanish established Isabella on Hispaniola in 1493 during Columbus's second voyage [d1], and Santo Domingo — described as the first European permanent settlement — was built in 1496 [d6]. The first permanent English settlement was at Jamestown, Virginia: colonists arrived in Chesapeake Bay in April 1607 [d4], with approximately 144 settlers and sailors landing on May 13, 1607 [d2][d8]. In the early 1600s more broadly, the English founded Jamestown in 1607, the French built Quebec in 1608, and the Dutch began their own settlements shortly after [d9]. For the specific colony of Georgia, the first settlers arrived in 1733 [d3][d7].
